title: WSM: Decay-Free Learning Rate Schedule via Checkpoint Merging for LLM Pre-training
authors: Changxin Tian*, Jiapeng Wang*, Qian Zhao*, Kunlong Chen, Jia Liu, Ziqi Liu, Jiaxin Mao, Wayne Xin Zhao, Zhiqiang Zhang, Jun Zhou (* equal contribution)
lab: Ling Team, Ant Group; Gaoling School of Artificial Intelligence, Renmin University of China
date: v1 23 July 2025; v2 11 August 2025 (adds citations of Hägele et al. 2024; no number changes). Added to the knowledge base 2026-08-31 on request
run_label: train the toy in your browser
takeaway: Proves checkpoint merging is algebraically equivalent to LR decay (merge weights invert to per-step gradient weights), so a constant LR plus a weighted merge of the last n checkpoints emulates cosine, linear, or 1-sqrt decay with no decay phase at all; beats a matched WSD anneal by ~1.3 points on a 16.3B MoE, with merge duration the dominant hyperparameter and EMA merging the worst.
verdict: Believe the algebra and the recipe: keep the learning rate flat, save checkpoints, average the last stretch, and you get about what a decay gives, plus a cheap preview of the decayed model. Treat the size of the win as provisional: the +1.28 points is +1.18 at matched tokens, every comparison is one run with the best checkpoint picked on the test benchmarks, and the paper's merge-shape ranking reverses at matched tokens.

resources.t: Scaling Laws and Compute-Optimal Training Beyond Fixed Training Durations (Hägele et al., arXiv 2405.18392)
resources.by: Alexander Hägele, Elie Bakouch, Atli Kosson, Loubna Ben Allal, Leandro von Werra, Martin Jaggi
resources.n: background on why the decay phase is worth attacking: constant LR plus a short cooldown matches cosine, the 1-sqrt cooldown beats linear, and weight averaging as a partial substitute.

resources.t: Model Merging in Pre-training of Large Language Models (Li et al., arXiv 2505.12082)
resources.n: the concurrent, purely empirical take: WMA, SMA and EMA merging during constant-LR pretraining, reaching the performance of an annealed model.

resources.t: Understanding Warmup-Stable-Decay Learning Rates: A River Valley Loss Landscape Perspective (Wen et al., arXiv 2410.05192)
resources.by: Kaiyue Wen, Zhiyuan Li, Jason Wang, David Hall, Percy Liang, Tengyu Ma
resources.n: the river-valley picture behind the paper's canyon-and-river analogy (§4.4): a high constant LR makes progress along the river while bouncing between the canyon walls; decay or averaging settles onto the floor.

resources.t: The Road Less Scheduled (Defazio et al., arXiv 2405.15682)
resources.by: Aaron Defazio, Xingyu Yang, Harsh Mehta, Konstantin Mishchenko, Ahmed Khaled, Ashok Cutkosky
resources.n: schedule-free optimisation: deletes the schedule by iterate averaging inside the optimiser, where WSM does it outside, on saved checkpoints.

resources.t: Every Activation Boosted: Ling 2.0 technical report (arXiv 2510.22115), §3.2.3
resources.n: the same lab's production use of WSM for Ling-mini-2.0, Ling-flash-2.0 and Ling-1T, plus the top-32-by-validation checkpoint average it added on top.

kb.n: Llama 3 405B annealed the LR linearly to 0 on its last 40M tokens and averaged checkpoints during the anneal (§3.4.3): exactly the Decay-then-Merge hybrid that WSM found adds nothing (Figure 5b).

keeps an EMA of the weights in CPU memory "for early estimation of the model performance after learning rate decay" (§3.2.3): WSM's evaluation-proxy use, already in production, with the EMA shape WSM ranks last.
why cosine needs the run length up front: a cosine cycle longer than the run leaves the LR high at the end, which is how Chinchilla explained part of the gap to Kaplan's laws (Appendix B).

kb.t: Scaling Laws for Neural Language Models
kb.n: the cosine-to-zero schedules WSD and WSM were designed to replace.
model souping at the end of mid-training: the same weight-averaging machinery, used as ensembling rather than as a schedule.

topics.n: Optimisers and learning-rate schedulers: the LR-schedule family (cosine, WSD, schedule-free, WSM) and where the WSD-versus-WSM comparison lives.
Pretraining and Data mixing: WSM's data-anneal switch step is the same lever as the mid-training anneal (Dolmino, Llama 3 annealing).
the Olmo 3 recipe's checkpoint souping, with its public training logs.
